original_text:
Cybersecurity is the practice of protecting computer systems, networks, and digital information from unauthorized access, attacks, and data breaches. As organizations increasingly rely on digital technologies, cybersecurity has become a critical component of business operations and national security.

Common cyber threats include malware, ransomware, phishing attacks, password theft, insider threats, and distributed denial-of-service attacks. Cybercriminals continuously develop new techniques to exploit software vulnerabilities and compromise sensitive information.

Organizations implement multiple layers of security, including firewalls, antivirus software, encryption, multi-factor authentication, intrusion detection systems, and regular software updates. Employee awareness training is also essential because human error remains one of the leading causes of security incidents.

Governments, businesses, and technology companies collaborate to establish cybersecurity standards, share threat intelligence, and develop stronger defense mechanisms. As digital transformation continues, cybersecurity professionals play an increasingly important role in protecting critical infrastructure, financial systems, healthcare organizations, and personal information from evolving cyber threats.
